delivery.summary: This matches a documented delivery/customs impersonation warning pattern.
actions: Do not pay, reply, or open any link in the message.
Check the parcel by opening the courier's official website or app yourself (type the address or use the app you already have).
If the message claims to be from a customs authority, contact that authority only through its official website or channels.
Report impersonation to the organisation being impersonated (for DHL: phishing@dhl.com, with a screenshot that shows the sender number).
delivery.official_route: Open the courier's official site or app manually; do not use the link in the message.

banking.summary: This matches a documented bank/central-bank impersonation warning pattern.
actions: Do not reply, and never share card numbers, PINs, passwords or security codes.
Contact your bank only through the number on its official website or on your card, never a number or link from the message.
Report bank-related fraud to your bank and through official UAE fraud-reporting channels.
banking.official_route: Use your bank's official app or the contact number printed on your card.

url_caution.summary: No documented message pattern matched, but a link in the message has suspicious characteristics.
actions: If the message concerns a real account or parcel, go to that organisation's official website or app yourself.
url_caution.official_route: Navigate to the organisation's official site manually.

no_match.summary: Nothing in this message matches a documented pattern. That is not a guarantee.
actions: If the message asks for money, codes or personal details, or creates urgency, verify through an official channel before acting.
Never use links or phone numbers from the message itself to verify it.
no_match.official_route: Verify through the organisation's official website, app, or the number on your card.

out_of_scope.summary: The desk has no documented pattern for this kind of message, so it can't tell you either way.
actions: Don't pay, send money, or share IDs or codes because of this message.
Check with the organisation directly through its official website, app, or a number you already trust.
If it claims to be from the police, a ministry or an employer, contact them yourself instead of replying.
out_of_scope.official_route: Verify through the organisation's official website or app, never through the message.

job_visa.summary: This matches a documented job/visa warning pattern from the UAE Government portal.
actions: Do not pay any fee, send a deposit, or share your passport or bank details because of this message.

Check that a real job offer exists: the UAE Government portal says an offer must be issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE), and that you can check its reference number on MOHRE's enquiry service.
Check that the company legally exists in the National Economic Register.
Do not travel or start work on a visit or tourist visa: it does not give the right to work in the UAE.
Contact MOHRE through its official website, ask@mohre.gov.ae or the number on that website, not any contact in the message.
job_visa.official_route: Open the MOHRE website or app yourself and look up the offer.
